Anatomy-02.question: ১) The notochord is formed by the cells of the –
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is mesoderm. The notochord develops from axial mesoderm during gastrulation.

Key points:

  • Notochord is derived from mesodermal cells in the midline.

  • It acts as an important signalling structure for:

    • Neural tube formation

    • Vertebral column development (later replaced by vertebral bodies, with remnants forming the nucleus pulposus)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Hypoblast → Contributes to extraembryonic structures; does not form notochord.

  • Endoderm → Forms epithelial linings of the gut and respiratory tract.

  • Neuroectoderm → Forms the neural tube and nervous system.

High-yield embryology:

Germ layer Main derivatives
Mesoderm Notochord, bone, muscle, connective tissue
Ectoderm Nervous system, epidermis
Endoderm Gut and respiratory epithelium

Exam pearl:
Notochord = axial mesoderm derivative.

Anatomy-02.question: ২) The structures representing all three components of embryonic disc is
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is tympanic membrane. The tympanic membrane is derived from all three germ layers of the embryonic disc.

Embryonic disc components:

  • Ectoderm → External epithelial lining

  • Mesoderm → Fibrous connective tissue layer

  • Endoderm → Internal epithelial lining

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Meninges → Mainly derived from neural crest and mesoderm, not all three germ layers.

  • Retina → Derived from neuroectoderm only.

  • Pituitary gland → Derived from ectoderm:

    • Adenohypophysis → Oral ectoderm (Rathke’s pouch)

    • Neurohypophysis → Neuroectoderm

High-yield embryology:

Structures with ectoderm + mesoderm + endoderm contribution:

  • Tympanic membrane

  • Some pharyngeal membrane derivatives

Exam pearl:
Tympanic membrane = ectoderm + mesoderm + endoderm.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩) Human placenta is -
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is haemochorial. In humans, the placenta is haemochorial because maternal blood is in direct contact with the chorionic trophoblast.

Placental types (based on layers separating maternal and fetal blood):

Type Example
Epitheliochorial Pig, horse
Endotheliochorial Dog, cat
Haemochorial Human, primates
Haemoendothelial Some rodents

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epitheliochoreal → Seen in animals like pigs and horses.

  • Haemoendothelial → Maternal blood directly contacts fetal capillary endothelium (not humans).

  • Endothelialchoreal → Seen in carnivores (e.g., dogs).

Exam pearl:
Human placenta = haemochorial placenta.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪) The fetal membrane that is ruptured during labor –
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is amnion. During labour, rupture of the amnion (together with the chorion) causes rupture of membranes and release of amniotic fluid ("water breaking").

Key points:

  • Fetal membranes:

    • Amnion → Inner membrane surrounding amniotic fluid

    • Chorion → Outer fetal membrane

  • At term, amniochorionic membrane ruptures during labour.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Amniochorionic membrane → Actually the combined membrane that ruptures, but the amnion is the fetal membrane classically described as ruptured in this MCQ.

  • Chorion → Outer membrane; not the main membrane referred to in rupture of membranes.

  • Decidua → Maternal endometrial tissue, not a fetal membrane.

High-yield obstetrics:

Rupture of membranes (ROM) = rupture of amnion + chorion → release of amniotic fluid

Exam pearl:
“Water breaking” = rupture of amniotic membrane.

Anatomy-02.question: ৫) Fate of notochord –
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is nucleus pulposus of intervertebral disc. The notochord persists as the nucleus pulposus after vertebral development.

Key points:

  • Notochord → Nucleus pulposus

  • Annulus fibrosus → Derived from surrounding mesoderm (sclerotome)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Cruciate ligament → Derived from mesenchymal tissue of the cervical region.

  • Annulus fibrosus of intervertebral disc → Derived from sclerotomal mesoderm, not the notochord.

  • Ligament of Berry → Thyroid suspensory ligament, not related to notochord.

High-yield embryology:

Structure Origin
Nucleus pulposus Notochord
Annulus fibrosus Sclerotome (mesoderm)

Exam pearl:
Notochord remnant = nucleus pulposus of intervertebral disc.

Anatomy-02.question: ৬) Number of gametes produced per germ cell during spermatogenesis?
৭) Ventral component of otic vesicle gives rise to
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is cochlear duct. The ventral part of the otic vesicle (otocyst) develops into the cochlear duct, which is responsible for hearing.

Development of otic vesicle:

  • Ventral component (saccular part)
    → Cochlear duct (organ of Corti develops inside it)

  • Dorsal component (utricular part)
    → Utricle, semicircular canals, endolymphatic duct

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Utricle → Derived from dorsal part of otic vesicle.

  • Semicircular canals → Derived from dorsal component.

  • Endolymphatic duct → Derived from dorsal component.

High-yield embryology:

Otic vesicle part Derivatives
Ventral (saccular) Cochlear duct
Dorsal (utricular) Utricle, semicircular canals, endolymphatic duct

Exam pearl:
Ventral otic vesicle → cochlear duct (hearing).

Anatomy-02.question: ৮) When spermatogenesis begins?
৯) Morula stage occurs at day
১০) During fusion with sperm cell membrane the stage of oocyte is
১১) Metencephalon forms
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is cerebellum. Metencephalon is a part of the hindbrain (rhombencephalon) and gives rise to the cerebellum and pons.

Development of brain vesicles:

Secondary brain vesicle Derivatives
Metencephalon Cerebellum + Pons
Myelencephalon Medulla
Diencephalon Thalamus + Hypothalamus
Mesencephalon Midbrain

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Medulla → Derived from myelencephalon.

  • Thalamus → Derived from diencephalon.

  • Hypothalamus → Derived from diencephalon.

Exam pearl:
Metencephalon = Cerebellum + Pons.

Anatomy-02.question: ১২) Commonest site of ectopic pregnancy
১৩) Neural crest derivatives exclude
১৪) Normal site of fertilization
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is ampulla of the uterine tube. Fertilization normally occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube, where sperm meets the secondary oocyte.

Key points:

  • Site: Ampulla of uterine (fallopian) tube

  • Timing: Usually within 24 hours after ovulation

  • The fertilised ovum then travels to the uterus for implantation.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Abdominal cavity → Abnormal site; may occur in abdominal ectopic pregnancy.

  • Uterine cavity → Site of implantation, not fertilization.

  • Isthmus → Narrow part of tube; not the usual site of fertilization.

High-yield embryology:

Fertilization = Ampulla
Implantation = Uterine endometrium

Exam pearl:
Normal site of fertilization → Ampulla of uterine tube.

Anatomy-02.question: ১৫) Fates of Mullerian duct in male
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is prostatic utricles. In males, the Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts regress due to anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) from Sertoli cells, leaving small remnants such as the prostatic utricle.

Fate of Müllerian duct in male:

  • Prostatic utricle (remnant)

  • Appendix testis

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Appendix of epididymis → Derived from mesonephric (Wolffian) duct remnants.

  • Ejaculatory duct → Derived from Wolffian duct.

  • Ductus deferens → Derived from Wolffian duct.

High-yield embryology:

Duct Male derivatives
Müllerian duct Prostatic utricle, appendix testis (remnants)
Wolffian duct Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle, ejaculatory duct

Exam pearl:
Male Müllerian duct remnant = Prostatic utricle.

Anatomy-02.question: ১৬) Days required for spermatogenesis
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is 74 days. Spermatogenesis takes approximately 74 days for the development of mature spermatozoa from spermatogonia.

Key points:

  • Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of testes.

  • Duration:

    • Spermatogenesis: ~74 days

    • Additional time for maturation and transport through epididymis: ~10–14 days

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 60 days → Less than the usual duration.

  • 70 days → Approximate but not the standard value.

  • 84 days → Longer than the accepted duration.

High-yield male reproduction:

Spermatogenesis = ~74 days
Starts at puberty and continues throughout life

Exam pearl:
Time required for spermatogenesis = 74 days.

Anatomy-02.question: ১৭) C cells of thyroid gland are derived from
১৮) Cornea is derived from
১৯) Structures of face formed from maxillary prominence
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is lateral portion of upper lip. The maxillary prominences form the lateral parts of the upper lip, upper cheek, and most of the maxilla.

Derivatives of facial prominences:

Facial prominence Derivatives
Maxillary prominence Lateral upper lip, upper cheek, maxilla, zygomatic bone
Medial nasal prominence Intermaxillary segment, philtrum of upper lip, bridge of nose
Lateral nasal prominence Ala of nose
Mandibular prominence Lower lip and mandible

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Bridge of nose → Derived from medial nasal prominences.

  • Lower lip → Derived from mandibular prominences.

  • Ala of nose → Derived from lateral nasal prominences.

Exam pearl:

Maxillary prominence → lateral upper lip.

Anatomy-02.question: ২০) Motor neuron is derived from
২১) Intermediate mesoderm derivative
২২) Cartilage is derived from
২৩) Central tendon of diaphragm develops from
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is septum transversum. The central tendon of the diaphragm develops from the septum transversum, which is derived from mesoderm.

Development of diaphragm:

  • Septum transversum → Central tendon

  • Pleuroperitoneal membranes → Posterolateral diaphragm

  • Dorsal mesentery of oesophagus → Crura of diaphragm

  • Muscular ingrowth from body wall → Peripheral muscular parts

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Lateral plate mesoderm → Contributes to body wall structures but not the central tendon.

  • Intermediate mesoderm → Forms urinary and reproductive systems.

  • Dorsal mesogastrium → Forms greater omentum, not diaphragm.

High-yield embryology:

Diaphragm component Origin
Central tendon Septum transversum
Crura Dorsal mesentery of oesophagus
Muscular part Body wall mesoderm

Exam pearl:
Septum transversum → central tendon of diaphragm.

Anatomy-02.question: ২৪) Notochord is derived from
২৫) Midgut is supplied by
২৬) Number of blastomeres in Morula –
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is 16. Morula is a solid ball of approximately 16 blastomeres formed after repeated cleavage divisions of the zygote.

Key points:

  • Day 3 after fertilisation → Morula stage

  • Contains about 16–32 blastomeres

  • Later develops into a blastocyst around day 5

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 8 blastomeres → Earlier cleavage stage (around day 3 before morula formation).

  • 12 blastomeres → Transitional stage, not the typical definition of morula.

  • 18 blastomeres → Within possible range, but the standard exam answer is 16.

High-yield embryology:

Stage Approximate cell number Time
Cleavage 2–8 cells Days 1–2
Morula 16 blastomeres Day 3
Blastocyst >100 cells Day 5

Exam pearl:
Morula = 16-cell stage (day 3).

Anatomy-02.question: ২৭) Normal site of Implantation:
Anatomy-02.option1: Anterior or posterior wall of body of uterus
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is anterior or posterior wall of the body of uterus. Normal implantation occurs in the upper part of the uterine cavity, usually on the posterior or anterior wall of the body/fundus of the uterus.

Key points:

  • Normal site: Upper posterior wall of uterus (most common)

  • Implantation occurs in the endometrium after the blastocyst reaches the uterus.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Abdominal cavity (Pouch of Douglas) → Abnormal site of ectopic implantation.

  • Fallopian tube → Common site of ectopic pregnancy, not normal implantation.

  • Internal os → Low implantation may cause placenta praevia.

High-yield embryology:

Fertilization → Ampulla of uterine tube
Implantation → Posterior wall of upper uterus

Exam pearl:
Normal implantation site = posterior wall of body/fundus of uterus.

Anatomy-02.question: ২৮) Most common site of ectopic pregnancy is
Anatomy-02.option4: Ampullary region of the uterine tube
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is ampullary region of the uterine tube. The ampulla is the most common site of ectopic pregnancy, accounting for the majority of tubal ectopic pregnancies.

Key points:

  • Common sites of ectopic pregnancy:

    • Ampulla of fallopian tube → most common (~70%)

    • Isthmus → second most common

    • Fimbrial end and interstitial part → less common

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Ovary → Rare site of ectopic pregnancy.

  • Abdominal cavity → Very rare; abdominal pregnancy is uncommon.

  • Intramural (interstitial) part of uterine tube → Less common than ampullary ectopic pregnancy.

High-yield embryology:

Site Frequency
Ampullary region of uterine tube Most common
Isthmus Second most common
Interstitial part Rare

Exam pearl:
Most common site of ectopic pregnancy = Ampulla of fallopian tube.

Anatomy-02.question: ২৯) The process that establishes all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm) in the embryo is called-
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is gastrulation. Gastrulation is the process during embryonic development that converts the bilaminar embryonic disc into a trilaminar disc by forming the three primary germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.

Key points:

  • Occurs during third week of development

  • Formation of:

    • Ectoderm → nervous system, epidermis

    • Mesoderm → muscle, bone, connective tissue, cardiovascular system

    • Endoderm → epithelial lining of gut and respiratory tract

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Implantation → Attachment of blastocyst to the uterine endometrium.

  • Blastomere formation → Cleavage process producing early embryonic cells.

  • Embryogenesis → General term for formation and development of the embryo, not specifically germ layer formation.

High-yield embryology:

Gastrulation = formation of three germ layers
Timing: 3rd week of embryonic development

Exam pearl:
Ectoderm + Mesoderm + Endoderm formation → Gastrulation.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩০) Cells that form the three primitive germ layers are derived from the –
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is epiblast. All three primitive germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm) are derived from epiblast cells during gastrulation.

Key points:

  • During gastrulation (3rd week):

    • Epiblast cells migrate through the primitive streak.

    • They form:

      • Endoderm → replaces hypoblast

      • Mesoderm

      • Ectoderm → remaining epiblast cells

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Cytotrophoblast → Forms part of the chorionic trophoblast and contributes to placenta.

  • Hypoblast → Contributes mainly to extraembryonic endoderm (yolk sac lining), not the definitive germ layers.

  • Yolk sac → Extraembryonic structure; does not form the three germ layers.

High-yield embryology:

Epiblast → ectoderm + mesoderm + endoderm

Exam pearl:
All definitive embryonic tissues arise from epiblast.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩১) Mesoderm showing segmentation is -
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is paraxial mesoderm. Paraxial mesoderm undergoes segmentation to form somites during embryonic development.

Key points:

  • Paraxial mesoderm → Somites

    • Sclerotome → Vertebrae and ribs

    • Myotome → Skeletal muscle

    • Dermatome → Dermis

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Intermediate mesoderm → Forms the urinary and genital systems (kidneys and gonads).

  • Lateral plate mesoderm → Forms heart, blood vessels, body wall, and limb connective tissues.

  • Splanchnic mesoderm → Part of lateral plate mesoderm; forms visceral structures and cardiovascular tissues.

High-yield embryology:

Paraxial mesoderm = segmented mesoderm → somites

Exam pearl:
Only paraxial mesoderm shows segmentation.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩২) Hindgut derivative
৩৩) Nerve for 3rd pharyngeal arch
৩৪) The series of changes resulting in the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa-
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is spermiogenesis. Spermiogenesis is the process by which spermatids transform into mature spermatozoa without further cell division.

Key points:

  • Spermatogenesis = Entire process of sperm formation:

    • Spermatogonia → spermatocytes → spermatids → spermatozoa

  • Spermiogenesis = Final maturation step:

    • Spermatids → spermatozoa

Changes during spermiogenesis:

  • Formation of acrosome

  • Development of flagellum (tail)

  • Nuclear condensation

  • Loss of excess cytoplasm

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Spermatogenesis → Broad process including all stages of sperm production, not specifically spermatid transformation.

  • Spermatocytosis → Refers to formation of spermatocytes, not maturation of spermatids.

High-yield embryology:

Spermatid → Spermatozoa = Spermiogenesis

Exam pearl:
No cell division occurs during spermiogenesis; it is a maturation process.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩৫) Primary oocyte is produced during
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is prenatal period. Primary oocytes are formed during fetal life before birth.

Key points:

  • Oogenesis begins during embryonic (fetal) life.

  • Primordial germ cells → oogonia → primary oocytes

  • Primary oocytes enter meiosis I and remain arrested in prophase I until puberty.

  • After puberty, one primary oocyte completes meiosis I during each menstrual cycle.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • After puberty → Completion of meiosis I occurs after puberty, not formation of primary oocytes.

  • Postnatal period before puberty → Primary oocytes are already formed before birth and remain arrested.

  • None of above → Incorrect.

High-yield oogenesis:

Fetal life → Primary oocyte formation
Puberty → Completion of meiosis I → Secondary oocyte formation

Exam pearl:
Primary oocytes are produced during prenatal (fetal) life.

Anatomy-02.question: ৩৬) Stylopharyngeus muscle is derived from which pharyngeal arch?
৩৭) Derivative of 3rd pharyngeal pouch
৩৮) Inferior parathyroid gland is derived from which pharyngeal pouch?
৩৯) Pulmonary trunk is derived from
৪০) Which layer of uterus are considered for implant of blastocyst?
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is endometrium. The blastocyst implants into the endometrial lining of the uterus, specifically the functional layer (stratum functionale).

Layers of uterus:

  • Endometrium → Inner mucosal layer; site of implantation

  • Myometrium → Smooth muscle layer responsible for uterine contractions

  • Perimetrium → Outer serosal covering

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Perimetrium → Outer covering of uterus; not involved in implantation.

  • Myometrium → Muscular layer beneath endometrium.

  • Epimetrium → Not a recognised anatomical layer of the uterus.

High-yield embryology:

Blastocyst implantation = Endometrium (decidua formation)

Exam pearl:
Implantation occurs in the endometrial lining of the uterus.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪১) Diploid number of chromosomes are found in
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is zygote. A zygote is diploid (2n) because it is formed by the fusion of haploid spermatozoa and haploid oocyte.

Chromosome number:

  • Oocyte (secondary oocyte) → Haploid (n = 23)

  • Spermatozoa → Haploid (n = 23)

  • Spermatid → Haploid (n = 23)

  • Zygote → Diploid (2n = 46)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Oocyte → Contains a haploid set of chromosomes after meiosis I.

  • Spermatozoa → Haploid male gamete.

  • Spermatid → Haploid cell formed after meiosis II.

High-yield embryology:

Sperm (n) + Oocyte (n) → Zygote (2n = 46 chromosomes)

Exam pearl:
Diploid chromosome number is restored at fertilisation in the zygote.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪২) Central tendon of diaphragm is developed from
৪৩) When the zona pellucida are disappeared?
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is allowing implantation to begin. The zona pellucida disappears (zona hatching) around day 5 after fertilisation, allowing the blastocyst to attach to the endometrium and implantation to start.

Key points:

  • Fertilised ovum is surrounded by zona pellucida during early cleavage.

  • Blastocyst hatching occurs before implantation.

  • Loss of zona pellucida allows:

    • Attachment to uterine endometrium

    • Trophoblast invasion

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Allowing implantation to end → Implantation begins after zona pellucida disappearance, not ends.

  • Before blastocyst formation → Zona pellucida is still present during cleavage and blastocyst formation.

  • During morula formation → Morula remains enclosed within zona pellucida.

High-yield embryology:

Day 5: Blastocyst hatching → Zona pellucida disappears → Implantation begins

Exam pearl:
Zona pellucida disappears before implantation to allow blastocyst attachment.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪৪) What is the normal site of implantation?
Anatomy-02.option2: Anterior or posterior wall of the body of the uterus
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is anterior or posterior wall of the body of the uterus. Normal implantation occurs in the upper part of the uterine cavity, usually on the posterior wall (most common) or anterior wall of the body of the uterus.

Key points:

  • Implantation site: Endometrium of upper uterus

  • Most common: Posterior wall of uterine body near fundus

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Fundus of uterus → Can be a site of implantation, but the standard description is the anterior or posterior wall of the body of uterus.

  • Internal os of uterus → Low implantation may cause placenta praevia.

  • Cornua of uterus → Unusual site; may be associated with interstitial ectopic pregnancy.

High-yield embryology:

Normal implantation = posterior/anterior wall of body of uterus (upper uterine cavity)

Exam pearl:
Most common implantation site = posterior wall of upper body of uterus.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪৫) Definitive kidney develops from
৪৬) When the acrosome reaction occurs?
Anatomy-02.option1: After binding to the corona radiata
Anatomy-02.option2: Before binding to the corona radiata
Anatomy-02.option3: After binding to the zona pellucida
Anatomy-02.option4: Before binding to the zona pellucida
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is after binding to the zona pellucida. The acrosome reaction occurs when sperm binds to the zona pellucida (especially ZP3 receptors), leading to release of acrosomal enzymes that help sperm penetrate the zona pellucida.

Key points:

  • Sperm first passes through:

    1. Corona radiata

    2. Zona pellucida

  • Acrosome reaction occurs after zona pellucida binding

  • Enzymes released:

    • Acrosin

    • Hyaluronidase

The other options are incorrect because:

  • After binding to corona radiata → Sperm attachment to corona radiata occurs before acrosome reaction.

  • Before binding to corona radiata → Incorrect; sperm must reach and interact with the oocyte coverings.

  • Before binding to zona pellucida → Incorrect; zona pellucida binding triggers the acrosome reaction.

High-yield embryology:

Corona radiata penetration → Zona pellucida binding (ZP3) → Acrosome reaction → Fertilization

Exam pearl:
Acrosome reaction is triggered by sperm binding to zona pellucida.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪৭) Events of spermiogenesis excludes
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is flagella formation. Spermiogenesis is the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa and includes acrosome formation, nuclear condensation, and development of the neck, middle piece, and tail.

Events of spermiogenesis:

  • Acrosome formation from Golgi apparatus

  • Nuclear condensation

  • Formation of neck, middle piece, and tail

  • Loss of excess cytoplasm

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Acrosome formation → Occurs during spermiogenesis.

  • Nucleus condensation → Occurs during spermiogenesis.

  • Neck, middle piece & tail formation → Occurs during spermiogenesis.

Note: Flagellum (tail) develops from the centriole during spermiogenesis, so some textbooks consider it part of spermiogenesis. However, in standard embryology MCQs, "flagella formation" is often described as sperm structural development rather than a separate event of spermiogenesis.

Exam pearl:
Spermiogenesis = spermatid maturation → acrosome formation + nuclear condensation + tail formation.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪৮) Gametes are derived from -
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is primordial germ cells (PGCs). Gametes (sperm and ova) are derived from primordial germ cells, which originate from the epiblast and migrate to the yolk sac before reaching the developing gonads.

Key points:

  • Epiblast → Primordial germ cells

  • Primordial germ cells → Spermatogonia and oogonia

  • Spermatogonia → Spermatozoa

  • Oogonia → Oocytes

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Trophoblast → Forms fetal part of placenta.

  • Syncytiotrophoblast → Involved in implantation and hormone secretion (e.g., hCG).

  • Yolk sac → Site of early migration of primordial germ cells, but does not form gametes.

High-yield embryology:

Primordial germ cells → Gametes

Exam pearl:
Gamete precursor = primordial germ cells.

Anatomy-02.question: ৪৯) Site of spermatogenesis in male-
Anatomy-02.exp:
The correct answer is seminiferous tubule. Spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, where spermatogenic cells develop into spermatozoa.

Key points:

  • Site: Seminiferous tubules (testis)

  • Sertoli cells → Support sperm development

  • Leydig cells → Produce testosterone required for spermatogenesis

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Seminal vesicle → Produces fructose-rich seminal fluid; not involved in sperm formation.

  • Vas deferens → Transports sperm from epididymis to ejaculatory duct.

  • Epididymis → Site of sperm maturation and storage.

High-yield male reproduction:

Spermatogenesis = Seminiferous tubules
Sperm maturation = Epididymis

Exam pearl:
Site of spermatogenesis → Seminiferous tubules of testes.

Anatomy-02.question: ৫০) Implantation usually completes at day
